overview: The Community Development Board authorized city staff to prepare a scope of work to evaluate the linkage fee schedule, voted to recommend that the City Council accept Freedom Way and Steve Miller Way as public ways, and approved a linkage fee credit for sewer work at 23 Sycamore Ave. Staff and board members also discussed the Comprehensive Plan review process and upcoming project proposals.

items.title: Reassessment of Linkage Fee Schedule
items.summary: The board voted 5-0 to request that the Department of Planning, Development and Sustainability prepare a scope of work to hire a consultant to evaluate and update Medford's linkage fee schedule, with additional discussion on potentially adding stormwater impact fees to linkage.

items.title: Freedom Way Public Way Acceptance
items.summary: The board voted 5-0 to recommend that the City Council accept Freedom Way as a public way, allowing the city to access Chapter 90 funds for roadway repairs while board members requested pedestrian and traffic equity improvements.

items.title: Steve Miller Way Public Way Acceptance
items.summary: The board voted 5-0 to recommend that the City Council accept Steve Miller Way as a public way to enable the use of state and federal funds for roadway maintenance.

items.title: 23 Sycamore Ave Linkage Credit Application
items.summary: The board voted 4-0 to approve a linkage fee credit for Oxford Properties, offsetting approximately $68,000 in linkage fees against $134,000 in sewer line improvements on Sycamore Avenue.

items.title: Miscellaneous and Other Updates
items.summary: Staff briefed the board on upcoming proposals for 4060 Mystic Valley Parkway and the Great American Beer Hall, the newly released Climate Action Plan, and plans to schedule a dedicated meeting to review the draft Comprehensive Plan.
